title: Radioactivity and radiological hazards from a kaolin mining field in Ifonyintedo, Nigeria
author: Adagunodo, George, et al.

steps.title: Prepare equipment and verify specifications
steps.instruction: Gather the Super‑Spec RS‑125 hand‑held detector (manufactured by Canadian Geophysical Institute) and a GPSMAP 78 unit; confirm the detector uses a NaI(Tl) crystal, has an energy range of 0.80–1.2 MeV, and a quoted measurement error of about 5 %.

steps.title: Calibrate detector on test pads
steps.instruction: Perform the standard calibration on 1 × 1 m test pads as follows: accumulate spectra for 5 min on the potassium, thorium and uranium pads, then accumulate for 10 min on the background pad; apply the calibration equations Q00 (K % = 8.71 × RSI), Q11 (U ppm = 52.9 × RSI) and Q22 (Th ppm = 136.0 × RSI).

steps.title: Select survey locations
steps.instruction: Randomly choose eleven (11) measurement points across the upper axis of the kaolin deposit; record the latitude, longitude and elevation of each point using the GPSMAP 78.

steps.title: Acquire in‑situ radioactivity data
steps.instruction: At each of the 11 locations, perform four separate measurements with the detector set to assay mode; for each assay acquire a full count of 120 s, recording the displayed potassium (%), uranium (ppm), thorium (ppm) and gamma dose rate.

steps.title: Calculate location averages
steps.instruction: For each location, compute the mean and standard deviation of the four measurements for K‑40, Th‑232, U‑238 and the gamma dose rate.

steps.title: Convert to activity concentrations
steps.instruction: Convert the recorded K‑40, Th‑232 and U‑238 concentrations to becquerels per kilogram (Bq kg⁻¹) using the International Atomic Energy Agency conversion factors.
